steps.text: Place sausage in a large, deep skillet. Cook over medium-high heat until evenly brown. Drain and chop into bite-sized pieces; set aside.
While sausage is cooking, beat eggs and milk together.
Pour eggs into a griddle. Add cheese and cook until eggs are set.
Stir in sausage and serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Sausage, Egg, and Cheese Scramble
raw_recipe.description: A scramble of sausage and eggs with cheese makes a perfect breakfast or brunch. This simple, scrumptious recipe will become a family-favorite dish.
raw_recipe.name: Sausage, Egg, and Cheese Scramble

review.reviewBody: Simply delicious! I LOVE scrambled eggs for breakfast especially on a Sunday! It's a great way to start the day and when you add in some sausage and cheese....well it's downright tasty. I usually use milk or a bit of half and half to achieve fluffy scrambled eggs, but this was recipe called for a bit too much. I used a bit less than 1/2 cup vs. 3/4 cup. I also like to add just pinch of onion and garlic powders plus a little salt and pepper. I used Cheddar cheese and served it with whole grain toast and "Home-Fried Potatoes" from this site. Next time, I might place every thing inside a warrm tortilla for a great breakfast wrap!

I've been doing something like this for years. I go a little further, I brown chopped tatters along with onion, bell pepper and mushrooms then add the eggs and last cheese. I cook this in a cast iron skillet on top of the stove over low heat covered for something like 7 minutes then shut off the heat and let it set for something like 5 minutes, cools it and it pulls away from the side of the skillet.

Great inspiration for a "Fridge clean-up" scrambled egg recipe! 1. Slice up (half-inch pieces) bacon and sausage and fry until done. 2. Add minced onions and garlic, then fry. 3. Add diced left-overs ( potatoes, carrots, veggies) plus eggs, grated cheese, salt and pepper. 4. Cook and serve. Never mind if some items are missing. Yum! And a different flavor with every cooking. This will be a weekly breakfast ritual!

Removed casing from sausage browned until no longer pink removed from skillet drained grease and scrambled eggs to our liked doneness. Served with side of grilled vegetables [red bell pepper bok choy asparagus] as a light dinner. Went over very well

This is a breakfast comfort food staple that can be left as is or add mushrooms, green peppers, etc. Usually, in the same cast iron skillet that the sausage is browning, I am also frying some country fries or hash browns. In a sauce pan I have some country pepper gravy or some sausage gravy cooking to spoon over the taters. The full breakfast then completes with the addition of a slice of lightly buttered (real butter) whole wheat toast and a cup of my favorite custom dark blend coffee. Ahhh heaven at the breakfast table!!!

So tasty! I made this with what I had on hand. After I cooked the sausage I took it out and added cut up red potatoes to sausage grease and cooked those up. I cut up the sausage into pieces in the meantime. When the potatoes were all cooked I added eggs to them then the sausage pieces. Topped with colby jack cheese. Yummy!!!!

We call this a "Breakfast Mess". I always have leftover home fries or hash brown potatoes. Even flavored rice. Those go in, and sometimes mushrooms, and chopped bacon instead of sausage. And chopped green onions as a garnish.
But I cook the meat and potatoes first, and then scramble the eggs into it. Then top with cheese and garnish. I add salsa.

Classic recipe and just how my mom used to make it. Always looking for low carb/low sugar and had some leftover Mables BBQ (Cleveland, OH) from the night before so I decided to jazz things up this morning.eggs (coconut milk, minced onion, garlic powder, salt, pepper), kielbasa, brisket, rib meat, collard greens and havarti cheese... Awesome!

Tender moist eggs and deliciously browned savory sausage. This is a great dish. I used regular Jimmy Dean sausage and made my own link shaped sausage logs. I am not fond of eggs but I can tolerate them in a dish with other things that mask them such as this dish, so I did scale back to only 1 egg for my serving, so the ratio of sausage was a little heavier on the sausage side than the recipe calls for. I thought it would be too much milk, but it wasn't after all, and it kept the eggs very moist and making them soft and custard-like. I did take the liberty of adding a little salt and pepper to my eggs before cooking them as I like them seasoned. It isn't stated, but I expect with any recipe that it's implied to season to taste, as common steps such as that may not be written, if everyone already knows to do it. It falls into the same category as breaking an egg open to use the contents. Everyone knows to do it, so it doesn't need to be indicated. This would be great wrapped in a tortilla for a meal on the go. Nice scramble. I cleaned my plate, egg and all.

Great recipe. I add one chopped green onion and 1/2 of dried dill to this recipe to enhance the flavour. Occasionally, I substitute chopped kielbasa for the pork sausage. I serve it on top of buttered toast to sop up any liquid with a side of sliced tomato and hash browns. Delicious!
I used 1/4 cup of heavy whipping cream and 1/4 cup of milk. This held the eggs together nicely. The original recipe of 3/4 cup milk is too much liquid.
This tastes really good and it's easy to prepare.
I didn't add milk, but it was really good. I am going to have some French toast tomorrow along with the eggs.
Really good with spicy Italian sausage and leftover baked potato...very flavorful!
I love it!
Very easy to make and flexible. I added onion, tomatoes, and topped with almond slivers. Added nice crunch. you can add whatever you like to have with your scrambled eggs.
I added chopped tomatoe and green onions and it was so tasty.
Simple and delicious! Added.some green onion and wrapped it in a tortilla. Thanks for sharing.
Such an easy, tasty and versatile breakfast fare. I'll add diced potatoes next time.
Made this today for me and my partner, adding some pepper and a few dried mixed herbs really compliments it all
